4 or more years of experience providing programs, services, and/or supervision related to gender equity, reproductive justice, or a related student or community services area

Under the direction of the Director of the Womxn’s Center for Success, the Senior Specialist, Womxn’s Center for Success is responsible for providing educational, inclusive, and student development-centered programs, initiatives, and involvement opportunities (through employment, internships, and/or service) that advance gender equity at UCI.

The Senior Specialist leads the coordination and management of reproductive justice, womxn’s health and wellbeing, and menstruation equity programs. Program coordination includes all aspects of the program development and implementation cycle, including planning, budget projection and tracking, logistics, task delegation, and assessment. Management of this area includes partnering with campus and community partners to provide equitable resources, remove barriers and expand accessibility, understand community needs, and increase awareness.

The Senior Specialist builds and sustains partnerships across the UCI campus community, including academic departments, student affairs units, and campus resource centers, to advance the development, enrichment, inclusion, and retention of womxn and female students across all disciplines. This work includes identifying opportunities for collaboration, co-developing programs and initiatives with campus partners, and representing the Center in cross-divisional efforts that support gender equality.
Flexibility to work evenings and weekends when necessitated by program requirements.
Thorough knowledge of advising and counseling techniques.
Strong knowledge of common University-specific computer application programs and knowledge of University and departmental principles and procedures involved in risk assessment.
Skills in judgment and decision-making, problem solving, identifying measures of system performance and the actions to improve performance.
Thorough knowledge of Student Affairs / Student Life specialization.
Abilities in project management, problem identification and reasoning skills.
Understanding of university, college, or city/county/state administrative organizations, policies, procedures, and practices.
Ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.

Demonstrated understanding of intersectionality of gender with race, ethnicity, culture, disability, sexual orientation, socio-economic status, religion/spirituality, and other social identity categories.
Demonstrated knowledge of social justice frameworks and gender equity principles, and ability to apply them to program development and student advising.
Skill in program organization, budget preparation and tracking, publicity and marketing, and evaluation.
Ability to develop and maintain collaborative partnerships with campus and community stakeholders.
